newsitem.title: EGYPT: Offer in Egypt Cement 10 times oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Offer in Egypt Cement 10 times oversubscribed.

text.p: A public offer of nine million shares in a new privately-owned Egyptian cement company was about 10 times oversubscribed, the agents said on Tuesday.
"Each applicant will get between nine and 9.5 percent of the number of shares applied for," an official at the National Bank of Egypt (NBE), told Reuters.

Investors submitted over 100,000 applications to buy some 100 million shares -- priced at 10 pounds ($3) each -- within 10 days of the offer in Egypt Cement (Qena), which closed on Tuesday after the minimum 10 day statutory period.
Investors had to pay only a quarter of the share value with the application plus an issue fee of 0.10 pounds a share.
The founders have said another 25 percent of the share value is to be paid within six months of the date of establishment.
The company will ask for the remaining half within a year.
Bank officials attributed the heavy demand for the shares to increased awareness of the equities market and high prices.
"People are encouraged by the cheap price, high share prices in general and increased public awareness," NBE investment manager Ibrahim Abdullah has told Reuters.
State-owned banks and insurance firms, including the NBE, hold at least 40 percent of the firm, which has a 300 million pound paid up capital.
The expected annual return on capital would be 10 percent, the founders added.
The cement sector is highly profitable in Egypt and cement firms are among the stock market blue chips.
